## Main sequence

```text
Verdict: fixable - 1 blocker

Pick one:
1. assess - post the review to the PR; then approve or stop, no repairs.
2. deliver - repair blockers, rebase on main, watch CI, repeat until merge is offered. [recommended]
3. stop - remove the worktree, leave the PR as is.

Not offered: deliver with nits (no nits).
Course holds until the final menu; `show evidence` prints the full record.
```

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Before rejected the course model outright: it mapped the numeric 2 to `review`, substituted a `fix` grant, kept the single 12:17 deadline with no own-push renewal, stopped at a BEHIND menu instead of syncing, offered `fix` at B without addressing base-only SHA movement, pushed the re-run at C outside the gate, and had no sync restore/lease heads at D, so every fact failed. After delivers the Change cleanly: numeric 2 persists `course: deliver` with 0/10 caps before writes, P1 and P2 are repaired in successive waves with fresh helpers and reviewer closure and no intermediate menu, the table shows 12:17 → 12:25 → 12:27 renewals only on own pushes with the 12:11 base observation explicitly marked unchanged, BEHIND queues a Loop sync with its own checkpoint and the final menu offers merge without executing it, B and C exit `stuck - red twice without a source change` with exactly one re-run at C and no repair, and D persists `pre_head = B` and `expected_remote_head = A`, leases against A, and restores B after one refused push. All six facts hold; keep this wording. One small tightening for durability: in the B table, state the exit reason as 'base-only SHA movement does not satisfy the repair-wave source-change rule' in those words so the rule, not just its consequence, is visible to a reader.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After delivers the course model well: the single numeric 2 persists deliver, P1 and the CI-minted P2 are closed without a mid-sequence menu, BEHIND triggers the sync automatically, final offers merge without executing it, B and C exit stuck on repeated red with the base-sync/re-run distinctions stated, and D records expected_remote_head A, pre_head B, a lease against A, and a clean restore to B with no second push. The one miss is f2: the table sets the poll deadline to null after the 12:02 push (and null-then-12:25 after 12:10) on the reasoning that no watch starts while a blocker is open, whereas the fact expects every own push to mint a 15-minute window (12:17, 12:25, 12:27) regardless of whether a watch is immediately entered. To keep this, word the timeout rule so that an own push always records poll_deadline = push time + timeout (the watch may simply not be entered yet), and reserve null only for the pre-push state; keep the explicit note that the 12:11 base observation renews nothing. Before held nothing because it rejected the assess/deliver menu outright, so no regression occurred on the other facts.
